question: Will something outside the OEM stop a part or a shipping route for more than 30 days before 2031?
end_a: No. Every measure costs money but stays inside the 30-day limit. Tariffs, payment friction and customs time raise the bill without stopping anything for more than 30 days.
end_b: Yes. A producer country puts wire, niobium or cold heads under export control, an entity listing cuts the flow of parts through the China plant, or a sole supplier's owner leaves the MR business.
lean_sentence: The indicators lean weakly toward no. On 11 Oct 2026 the Section 232 investigation into medical products (a United States national-security trade investigation) had produced no proclamation, the trade truce with China was holding until its notice date, and no export-control listing named superconducting wire or cold heads.
settles_a: The answer settles as no if the 2027 sourcing cycle closes with the China truce renewed, the Section 232 report limited to finished scanners, and no export-control listing of wire, niobium or cold heads.
settles_b: The answer settles as yes if a notice in the Federal Register, from China's Ministry of Commerce or from a producer country names any of those parts, if an entity listing (the United States adding a company to its export blacklist) names the China plant or its logic supplier, or if a parent company announces the sale or closure of the wire mill or the cold-head plant.

question: In 2031, will helium supply still decide whether a magnet ships?
end_a: Yes. The Gulf route stays impaired or allocated, most new builds are still conventional, and a sealed magnet still needs a helium delivery for cool-down and testing.
end_b: No. Helium returns to a buyers' market, or sealed magnets take most new builds with a small test draw, so the cold head becomes the part that keeps every magnet cold.
lean_sentence: The indicators lean clearly toward yes. In the latest daily count, on 4 Oct 2026, four ships crossed the Gulf strait against a typical 85 (International Monetary Fund PortWatch data). Helium is bought on allocation letters, and no 3 tesla sealed magnet has been cleared for sale in the United States.
settles_a: The answer settles as yes if a United States helium allocation or export rule is proposed, if repairs to Qatar's damaged helium plant slip past 2028, or if a sealed magnet's test draw is confirmed as the size of a full helium delivery.
settles_b: The answer settles as no if the Gulf strait reopens to insured shipping and the allocation letters stop, if a 3 tesla sealed magnet is cleared, or if the test draw is confirmed as one gas cylinder rather than a full delivery.
